title: Signing On For Duty
description: Covers procedures and checks required when signing on for duty in person.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What action would you take if you forget / lose your safety critical licence?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Contact depot manager ASAP. Arrange for a photocopy to be sent to your signing on point if forgotten. Arrange for replacement if lost. Must not drive without a valid licence with you.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: You can drive as long as you report it lost within 24 hours.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: A verbal confirmation from the manager is sufficient to drive.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Sign on as normal and arrange for the licence later.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Possession of a valid safety-critical licence is mandatory for driving. If forgotten, a temporary photocopy must be obtained before driving. If lost, a replacement process must be initiated, and driving is not permitted without the licence.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What relevant publications need checking when signing on?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Check STN, AW, W.O.N, P.O.N etc.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Only check the Weekly Operating Notice (WON).
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Check the rule book updates page.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Only Altered Workings (AW) need to be checked.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: When signing on, drivers must check for any new or relevant updates in the Special Traffic Notices (STN), Altered Workings (AW), Weekly Operating Notices (WON), and Periodical Operating Notices (PON).

knowledgeUnits.concept: What notice cases need to be checked?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Check late notice case, Train crew notice case, Roster notice case, Incident notice case and Low adhesion notice case.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Only the Roster notice case and Late notice case.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Only the Incident notice case if there was a recent event.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Check the main notice board for general company updates.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: A thorough check of all relevant notice cases is required at sign-on, including Late Notices, Train Crew Notices, Roster information, Incident reports, and Low Adhesion updates.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What is your understanding of the statement for readiness for duty?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Signing confirms compliance with D&A policy, fitness to drive, correct uniform, possession of relevant publications/licence, read notices, possession of equipment, signed for traction/route, and possession of spare glasses (if applicable).
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: It confirms you have arrived at the depot on time.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: It's mainly a declaration that you have read the rule book.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: It confirms you have checked the train you will be driving.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: The readiness statement is a formal declaration covering multiple critical aspects: fitness (D&A, rest), compliance (uniform, equipment, publications, licence, notices), and competence (traction/route sign-off).

knowledgeUnits.concept: What checks are needed for personal equipment?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Check you have your keys, watch, iPad (working), hand lamp (working) etc.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Ensure your mobile phone is fully charged.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Check the expiry date on your PTS card.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Verify your uniform is clean and tidy.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Before starting duty, drivers must check they have all necessary personal equipment and that key items like the watch, iPad (if used for duty), and hand lamp are functioning correctly.
